papers.title_in_file: MerLin Reproduces 18 QML Papers with Improved Accuracy
papers.version_note: The text is a local copy of a LinkedIn post by Javier Mancilla Montero (2026-09-15), a secondary report on arXiv:2602.11092, not the paper itself.
papers.what_it_is: A LinkedIn post that summarizes the MerLin paper's reproduction of 18 photonic and hybrid QML papers.

assertions.value: The post's author states that Quandela reproduced 18 state-of-the-art QML papers and that one of the headline claims did not survive.
quotes: Quandela reproduced 18 state-of-the-art QML papers. One of the headline claims did not survive.
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.

assertions.value: The post's author describes MerLin as a new open-source discovery engine for photonic and hybrid quantum machine learning that plugs optimized strong simulation of linear-optical circuits into PyTorch and scikit-learn, so quantum layers train end-to-end with regular autograd.
quotes: MerLin, a new open-source discovery engine for photonic and hybrid quantum machine learning.
It plugs optimized strong simulation of linear-optical circuits directly into PyTorch and scikit-learn, so quantum layers train end-to-end with regular autograd.
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.
assertions.reader_inference: The post's author is not Quandela; the description relays the MerLin paper's own framing.

assertions.value: The post's author states that the team reproduced 18 photonic and hybrid QML papers and released them as modular experiments.
quotes: The team reproduced 18 state-of-the-art photonic and hybrid QML papers, released them as modular experiments, and reported what actually held up:
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.

assertions.value: The post's author reports that the team improved the reported accuracy of a photonic QCNN from 92.7% to 98.2% on one dataset and from 93.1% to 98.8% on MNIST (0 vs 1), attributed to a proper hyperparameter study.
quotes: They improved the reported accuracy of a photonic QCNN from 92.7% to 98.2% on one dataset and from 93.1% to 98.8% on MNIST (0 vs 1) just by doing a proper hyperparameter study.
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.
assertions.reader_inference: The post does not name the unnamed first dataset or the hyperparameter ranges; verifying needs the MerLin paper.

assertions.value: The post's author reports that a photonic QGAN reproduction matched the original SSIM results while cutting training time by up to 15x, by switching from SPSA to plain PyTorch SGD.
quotes: A photonic QGAN reproduction matched the original SSIM results while cutting training time by up to 15x (switching from SPSA to plain PyTorch SGD).
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.

assertions.value: The post's author reports that a quantum LLM fine-tuning paper claimed up to a +3.14% accuracy gain, and that the reproduction found quantum and classical models all landing around 89%, with no clear separation.
quotes: A quantum LLM fine-tuning paper claimed up to a +3.14% accuracy gain.
The reproduction found quantum and classical models all landing around 89%, with no clear separation.
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.
assertions.reader_inference: This is probably the claim that 'did not survive', but the post does not say so; the link is an inference.

assertions.value: The post's author states that photonic work is only about 6% of QML publications and that code availability across QML papers hovers between 27% and 43%.
quotes: photonic work is only about 6% of QML publications, and code availability across QML papers hovers between 27% and 43%.
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.
assertions.reader_inference: No source is given in the post for either figure.

assertions.value: The post's author states that the field has been running on single-run metrics and unverifiable results for too long.
quotes: The field has been running on single-run metrics and unverifiable results for too long.
assertions.certainty_reason: A third-party LinkedIn post summarizing another paper; not the primary source.
assertions.reader_inference: Opinion of the post's author; no evidence is given in the post.

assertions.value: The post's author states that strong simulation caps out around 20 photons on standard hardware, so MerLin is a discovery and co-design tool for the near term, not a quantum advantage machine, and that the authors say so themselves.
quotes: Strong simulation caps out around 20 photons on standard hardware, so this is a discovery and co-design tool for the near term, not a quantum advantage machine.
The authors say so themselves

papers.version_note: arXiv:1710.11208v1 preprint of the Optics Letters paper; the text layer repeats the reference list.
papers.what_it_is: Experiment that creates SPDC photon pairs with one photon shaped into a finite-energy Airy mode by an SLM and shows its profile, parabolic path and preserved pair correlation by coincidence counting.

assertions.value: The authors state that the photon pairs are made by spontaneous parametric down conversion in a second periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide, with a pump at 779.83 nm producing signal and idler photons at 1554.7 nm and 1564.7 nm.
quotes: photon-pair generation via SPDC (779.83 nm → 1554.7 nm + 1564.7 nm)
the signal and idler photon pairs are picked at 1554.7 nm and 1564.7 nm respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own source configuration in the setup description.

assertions.value: The authors state that a continuous-wave laser at 1559.67 nm with a linewidth of at most 100 kHz is carved by an electro-optic modulator into a pulse train of 100 ps FWHM at 10 MHz repetition rate, and that second harmonic generation in a PPLN waveguide gives the SPDC pump pulses at 779.83 nm.
quotes: generates light at 1559.67 nm with ≤ 100 kHz linewidth
create a pulse train with 100 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) and 10 MHz repetition rate
phase matched to create SPDC pump pulses at 779.83 nm via second harmonic generation
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own pump configuration.

assertions.value: The authors state that both the idler and the signal photons are detected with InGaAs avalanche photodiodes (ID210, ID Quantique) with 10% quantum efficiency and fewer than 100 dark counts per second, and that each detection gives a TTL pulse to a multi-channel time-to-digital converter for coincidence measurement.
quotes: detected using an InGaAs avalanche photodiode (InGaAs APD)
with 10% quantum
< 100 dark counts per second
Each detected photon produces a TTL pulse which goes into a multi-channel time-to-digital converter (SENLS, HRM-TDC) for coincidence measurement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own detection setup.

assertions.value: The paper defines the two-dimensional transverse Airy mode as a product of two Airy functions in x and y with scaling factors x0 and y0 and an exponential truncation factor a (the equation of the mode), where Ai is the Airy function.
assertions.anchor: Equation of the transverse mode, p.2
quotes: where Ai stands for the Airy function, x0 and y0 are the scaling factors in x and y transverse directions, respectively, and a is a truncation factor [25].
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper defines the mode it generates.
assertions.reader_inference: The equation itself is garbled in the text layer; the value restates only the definition sentence.

assertions.value: The authors report that the experiment uses x0 = y0 = 271 µm, which corresponds to an Airy spatial mode with a main lobe of about 434 µm FWHM.
quotes: x0 = y0 = 271 µm which corresponds to an Airy spatial mode with a main lobe ∼ 434 µm FWHM
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states the design parameters of its own experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the cubic phase mask is created numerically on a 1.5 cm × 1.1 cm spatial light modulator (Santec SLM-100) over a 1.04 cm × 1.04 cm area with pixel size about 10.4 µm, followed by a Fourier transform lens, and that a linear phase along x is superposed to separate the first diffraction order from the unmodulated zeroth order.
quotes: 1.5 cm × 1.1 cm spatial light modulator (SLM) (Santec SLM-100)
discretizing the cubic phase over an 1.04 cm × 1.04 cm area (smaller than the SLM screen) with pixel size ∼ 10.4 µm
A linear phase modulation along the x direction is superposed on the cubic phase mask to de
thus separating it from any unmodulated light that will be in the zeroth order
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own modulation setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the total loss of the light through the free-space Airy-beam setup is 22 dB.
quotes: The total loss as the light go through the free-space setup is 22 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: One reported figure for one setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the coincident-to-accidentals ratio of the signal and idler photons, measured over an integration time of 60 minutes with 33 mW pump pulse peak power, is 69±6 without modulation and 70±3 with the Airy modulation.
quotes: is measured over an integration time of 60 minutes with 33 mW pump pulse peak power.
The CAR values in these two cases are 69±6 and 70±3, respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The two CAR values agree within error. A CAR comparison does not test the full two-photon state, for example its spatial entanglement or phase.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CAR values lie within each one's statistical error despite substantial loss in the setup, and conclude that the phase modulation by the SLM does not have any measurable impact on the quantum states of the photon pairs.
quotes: which are within each’s statistical error despite substantial loss in the current Airy-beam setup that reduces the photon counts
does not have any measurable impact on the quantum states of the photon pairs
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion drawn from one pair of CAR measurements.
assertions.reader_inference: The evidence is the CAR alone. No state tomography or entanglement test is reported.

assertions.value: The authors report that a pinhole line scan of the classical Airy beam gives a main lobe of about 500 µm FWHM, close to about 493 µm from the NIR-IR camera image and the theoretical value of about 434 µm.
quotes: measures the main lobe of the Airy beam to be ∼ 500 µm FWHM, close to the ∼ 493 µm value derived from NIR-IR camera image (Fig. 3, Inset) and the theoretical value of ∼ 434 µm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single measurement series.
assertions.reader_inference: The scan value is about 15 percent above the theoretical width; the paper calls it close.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pinhole was translated across a 2-mm range with a 50 µm step size, covering the main lobe and first side lobe, and that the intensity of higher order lobes is too low for this scanning measurement.
quotes: translated across a 2-mm range with a 50 µm step size, covering the Airy beam’s main lobe and the
The intensity of the higher order lobes is too low for this scanning measurement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states the limit of its own scan.

assertions.value: The authors report that the coincidence counts with the idler photons, scanned across the Airy signal photons with 0.2 W pump pulse peak power and a 600 second integration time per point, follow closely the profile of the classical Airy beam, which they take as verifying the Airy wavefunction of the signal photons. Error bars are the square root of the coincidence count.
quotes: at each scanning point the coincident counts are recorded with pump pulse peak power of 0.2 W for a 600second integration time.
thus verifying the Airy wavefunction of the signal photons.
the error bars are given as the square root of the coincidence count at each point.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one scan.
assertions.reader_inference: Only the main lobe and first side lobe were scanned, so the verification covers those lobes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Airy photons propagate for 3 meters along a parabolic, self-accelerating trajectory after the focal point of the Fourier lens.
quotes: those Airy photons propagate for 3 meters along a parabolic, self-accelerating trajectory.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own propagation distance.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 1-cm wide block inserted by 1.2 mm into the path cuts the power collected from a collimated Gaussian beam by 90% but the Airy beam by only 30%, and that the measured trajectories agree with a simulation using the exact SLM phase mask.
quotes: a 1-cm wide block is inserted into the path of Gaussian beam by 1.2 mm in the middle between the iris and
ber to drop by 90%.
causing only a 30% drop.
The good agreement between the simulation and measurement validates our entire setup.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single classical demonstration.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with 33 mW pump pulse peak power and a 60 minute integration time, inserting the block cut the total coincident counts of the Airy photons by 28%, which they state agrees with the Airy beam result, and that the CAR is 70±3 without and 62±4 with the block.
quotes: the pump pulse peak power is 33 mW and the integration time is 60 minutes.
the total coincident counts dropping by 28% when the blocked is inserted, which agrees with the results for the Airy beam.
The CAR values without and with the block are 70±3 and 62±4, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one run.
assertions.reader_inference: The CAR values differ by 8 with errors of 3 and 4, so a small drop with the block is not excluded. The paper gives no Gaussian-photon block measurement for comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that the potential of steering Airy photons on a controlled trajectory can be reconfigured in real time with a computer programmed SLM without any moving optics, and that this could be exploited for free-space quantum communications beyond line-of-sight.
quotes: by using a computer programmed SLM without any moving optics
This feature could be exploited for robust free-space quantum communications beyond line-of-sight [56].
assertions.certainty_reason: Prospective claim without a demonstration of real-time reconfiguration.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they created quantum correlated photons in a spatial Airy-shape wavefunction by spontaneous parametric down conversion and cubic spatial phase modulation, and found no observable degradation of the quantum states of the correlated photon pairs.
quotes: we have found that the spatial modulation on the photons does not introduce any observable degradation to the quantum states of the correlated photon pairs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Summary of the paper's own empirical results.

assertions.value: The authors state that the present experiment applies phase modulation directly on the generated photons, which induces loss and reduces the photon production rate, and that the lossless photon shaping technique of reference 62 could solve this in future research.
quotes: the present experiment applies phase modulation directly on the generated photons, which induces loss and
reduces the photon production rate.
This problem can be solved by using the lossless photon shaping technique demonstrated in [62]
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states the limit of its own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the earlier studies of Airy beams are all in the classical domain and that it remains to examine whether their advantages can be exploited in the quantum domain.
quotes: Those exciting studies, however, are all in the classical domain.
It remains to examine if those distinct advantages found in Airy beams could be exploited in the quantum domain
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim about the literature.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing reference 5, that Airy wave packets are a candidate for non-diffracting propagation along parabolic trajectories that mimic free acceleration.
quotes: Airy wave packets arose as a unique and promising candidate for their non-diffracting propagation along parabolic trajectories that mimic free acceleration [5].
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing references 8 to 10, that a common way to create Airy beams is spatial modulation of Gaussian beams with a cubic phase mask and a Fourier lens.
quotes: A common way to create the Airy beams is via spatial modulation of Gaussian beams using a cubic phase mask and a Fourier lens [8–10]
assertions.certainty_reason: Method attributed to other work.

papers.title_in_file: An Introduction to the Syntax and Content of Cyc
papers.what_it_is: A 2006 Cycorp overview of the CycL language and the OpenCyc and ResearchCyc ontologies, with example assertions.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Cyc project has spent the past twenty years, approximately 900 person-years of effort, building a knowledge base intended to capture a broad selection of common-sense background knowledge.
quotes: The Cyc project has spent the past twenty years— approximately 900 person-years of effort—building a knowledge base that is intended to capture a broad selection of common-sense background knowledge.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Cyc KB contains more than 2.2 million assertions describing more than 250,000 terms, including nearly 15,000 predicates.
quotes: The Cyc KB contains more than 2.2 million assertions (facts and rules) describing more than 250,000 terms, including nearly 15,000 predicates.
assertions.reader_inference: A 2006 snapshot; the paper gives no method for the count.

assertions.value: The authors state that the current version of OpenCyc includes an ontology of 47,000 terms, defined and elaborated using 306,000 assertions, and that this is a small subset of the total content of Cyc.
quotes: In its current version, OpenCyc includes an ontology of 47,000 terms, which are defined and elaborated using 306,000 assertions.

assertions.value: The authors state the thesis underlying Cyc: special-purpose domain systems can be brittle and difficult to extend to new or unforeseen problems.
quotes: these systems can be brittle [Friedland et al 2004] and difficult to extend to new or unforeseen problems or problem areas [Lenat 1995]
assertions.reader_inference: The brittleness claim is attributed to Friedland et al 2004 and Lenat 1995, not shown here.

assertions.value: The authors state that a primary goal of the Cyc project has been to build a large knowledge base of formalized background knowledge suitable for reasoning in a variety of domains.
quotes: a primary goal of the Cyc project has been to build a large knowledge base containing a store of formalized background knowledge suitable for supporting reasoning in a variety of domains
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the project goal in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that CycL's syntax expresses a number of extensions to first order logic, including a quoting mechanism that separates knowledge about a concept from knowledge about the term that denotes it.
quotes: CycL’s syntax expresses a number of extensions to first order-logic
It includes a quoting mechanism to enable differentiation between knowledge involving a concept, as opposed to knowledge about the term that expresses the concept.

assertions.value: The authors state that CycL has features of higher-order logics: quantification over predicates, functions and sentences, and predicates that take predicates as values, in some cases including themselves.
quotes: there is quantification over predicates, functions, and sentences,
and there is the ability for predicates to take predicates as values, including themselves in some cases.

assertions.value: The authors give an example of quoting: the ontology can hold that all dogs are mammals and also facts about the term #$Dog, such as when it was created and by whom.
quotes: such as when it was created and by whom

assertions.value: The authors state that quoting and higher-order extensions let the semantics of the language's terms be represented in the same language as all other knowledge, so that all knowledge has a common representational basis and is mutually accessible to inference.
quotes: so that all knowledge has a common representational basis and is mutually accessible to inference

assertions.value: The authors state that the higher-order features allow rule macro predicates, which give compact expressions of relationships that would otherwise require rules.
quotes: which allow for compact expressions of relationships that would otherwise require rules

assertions.value: The authors state that OpenCyc is a taxonomic projection of the Cyc Knowledge Base that primarily describes Cyc's taxonomic and definitional ontology, with class membership and subsumption expressed by isa and genls.
quotes: OpenCyc is, at heart, a taxonomic projection of the Cyc Knowledge Base
expressed with the predicates isa and genls, respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state what OpenCyc covers.

assertions.value: The authors state that a subsumption relationship exists among predicates, where the holding of one relation to some arguments implies the holding of another relation to those arguments, expressed via genlPreds.
quotes: where the holding of one relation to some set of arguments implies the holding of another relationship to those arguments (expressed via genlPreds)
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define genlPreds here.

assertions.value: The authors define a CycL sentence that conforms to the grammar but not to its semantic requirements as semantically ill-formed, and state that semantic well-formedness implements constraints on common-sense use of relationships and helps automate validation by rejecting the formal equivalents of ridiculous sentences.
quotes: If a CycL sentence conforms to the grammar but not its semantic requirements, it is said to be semantically ill-formed.
helps automate the validation of knowledge, by rejecting the formal equivalents of ridiculous sentences
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define the term in the text.

assertions.value: The authors give the example sentence 'Julia gave birth to a prime number' as grammatically well-formed but expressing a confused idea that could not be true in any context.
quotes: Julia gave birth to a prime number.
it expresses a confused idea that could not be true in any context
assertions.certainty_reason: Footnote 1 gives this as the authors' illustration.

assertions.value: The authors define the argument constraint as knowledge of what types of entities can be the values of a predicate or function, and give biologicalMother with the assertions isa IrreflexiveBinaryPredicate, arg1Isa Animal and arg2Isa FemaleAnimal.
quotes: The most basic type of definitional information is the argument constraint: knowledge of what types of entities can be the values of a predicate or function.
(isa biologicalMother IrreflexiveBinaryPredicate)
(arg2Isa biologicalMother FemaleAnimal)
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define the term and give the example.

assertions.value: The authors state that, rather than write a repetitive axiom for each irreflexive predicate, Cyc introduces the collection IrreflexiveBinaryPredicate, puts the logical feature in one axiom that references it, and makes new predicates instances of it.
quotes: the pattern of such an axiom is uselessly repetitive
expressing that logical feature in an axiom that references the collection, and making new predicates instances of the collection
assertions.reader_inference: The text states this as a design strategy; no measure of the saving is given.

assertions.value: The paper gives the CycL definitional axiom for arg1Isa: for all PRED, TYPE, X and VARS, if (arg1Isa PRED TYPE) and (PRED X VARS) hold then (isa X TYPE).
quotes: (forAll ?PRED (forAll ?TYPE (forAll ?X (forAll ?VARS (implies (and (arg1Isa ?PRED ?TYPE) (?PRED ?X ?VARS)) (isa ?X ?TYPE))))))
assertions.certainty_reason: The axiom is stated in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper states that genls is the basic sub-class predicate and the basis of the taxonomic hierarchy, is declared transitive and reflexive, and is defined by the axiom that if (genls TYPE1 TYPE2) and (isa X TYPE1) hold then (isa X TYPE2).
quotes: The predicate genls is the basic sub-class predicate and it is the basis of the taxonomic hierarchy.
(isa genls TransitiveBinaryPredicate) (isa genls ReflexiveBinaryPredicate)
(implies (and (genls ?TYPE1 ?TYPE2) (isa ?X ?TYPE1)) (isa ?X ?TYPE2))
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the definitional assertions and axiom.

assertions.value: The authors state that genls expresses inheritance among types and structures the ontology, while disjointWith states that two collections do not share any members.
quotes: while disjointWith states that two collections do not share any members
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define the predicate.

assertions.value: The authors state that comment, the main documentation predicate, has the assertions arg1QuotedIsa CycLIndexedTerm and arg2QuotedIsa SubLString, so its class restrictions apply to the terms themselves and not to the concepts they denote, which keeps ontology-management knowledge inside the ontology.
quotes: (arg1QuotedIsa comment CycLIndexedTerm) (arg2QuotedIsa comment SubLString)
so the class restrictions on the arguments are not relative to the concepts denoted by the terms, but to the terms themselves
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors give the assertions and the explanation.

assertions.value: The authors acknowledge a common criticism that most OpenCyc predicates are not fully populated and lack axiomatizing rules, grant that there is merit to it, and reply that a huge body of such knowledge is encoded in the definitional assertions.
quotes: A common criticism of OpenCyc is that although it includes a large number of predicates, most of those predicates are not fully ‘populated’
Although there is merit to those criticisms, they fail to acknowledge that a huge body of such knowledge is encoded in the definitional assertions
assertions.reader_inference: The reply is an argument by the OpenCyc authors, with no measurement.

assertions.value: The authors claim that taxonomic and definitional constraints are more efficient than ubiquitous axiomatization, and that a strong high-level ontology with inheritance allows a more efficient and thorough expression of common-sense facts than writing a rule.
quotes: Those constraints are more efficient than if they were to be ubiquitously axiomatized.
a strong ontology of high-level knowledge, with inheritance, allows for a more efficient and thorough expression of common sense facts
assertions.reader_inference: No efficiency measurement is reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that a fundamental distinction in the ontology is between collections and individuals, and that historical knowledge typically concerns individual events, countries and persons, while chemical and other scientific knowledge is typically described by properties of an entire class.
assertions.anchor: Content of the Cyc Ontology, p.3
quotes: One of the fundamental distinctions in the ontology is between collections and individuals.
chemical and other scientific knowledge is typically described in terms of the properties of an entire

assertions.value: The authors state that the upper ontology includes collections of collections, such as ExistingObjectType and ExistingStuffType, whose instances correspond to the count or mass interpretations of nouns.
assertions.anchor: Content of the Cyc Ontology, p.3
quotes: ExistingObjectType and ExistingStuffType are second-order collections whose instances correspond to the count or mass interpretations of nouns
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state what the collections are.

assertions.value: The authors state that the functional expression (SubcollectionOfWithRelationToFn Ambassador basedInRegion Turkey) denotes the collection of all ambassadors to Turkey.
assertions.anchor: Content of the Cyc Ontology, p.3
quotes: (SubcollectionOfWithRelationToFn Ambassador basedInRegion Turkey)
is the collection of all ambassadors to Turkey.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the meaning of the expression.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Cyc KB is traditionally divided into upper, middle and lower ontologies by level of generality; the upper is the smallest but most broadly referenced, the middle is widely used but not universal, and the lower holds domain-specific leaf-level knowledge and is the largest segment but least broadly applicable.
assertions.anchor: Upper, Middle, and Lower Cyc Ontology, p.3
quotes: The Cyc KB is traditionally subdivided into the upper, middle, and lower ontologies.
is the smallest but most broadly referenced area of the Cyc ontology
This layer accounts for the largest segment of knowledge in the KB, but the least broadly applicable.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define the three layers.

assertions.value: The paper states that Event is a specialization of Situation and that each instance of Event is a dynamic situation in which the state of the world changes, and that Events should not be confused with TimeIntervals.
quotes: Each instance of Event is a dynamic situation in which the state of the world changes
Events should not be confused with TimeIntervals.
assertions.certainty_reason: The comment assertion defines the term.

assertions.value: The paper lists assertions for Event including (genls Event Situation), (disjointWith Event PositiveDimensionalThing) and (genls HelicopterLanding Event), and marks the last as inferred knowledge.
quotes: (genls Event Situation)
(disjointWith Event PositiveDimensionalThing)
(genls HelicopterLanding Event) inferred knowledge
assertions.certainty_reason: The assertions are listed in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper states a rule that if an agent causes a Situation in some sense, the agent plays the role of causal actor, and a rule that if a situation provides a motive for an agent to play a role in a kind of event, the likelihood of that event increases.
quotes: If there is a situation that is caused (in some sense) by some agent, that agent plays the role of causal actor.
the likelihood of that event occurring increases
assertions.certainty_reason: The rules are given as example assertions in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper gives SocialGathering as a middle-ontology example: a specialization of SocialOccurrence with communication between participants, so that a group waiting to board an elevator is not typically a SocialGathering, with required actor slot attendees and a suggested dateOfEvent.
quotes: Note that a group of people waiting to board an elevator is not typically a SocialGathering
(requiredActorSlots SocialGathering attendees)
Although it is not semantically required, it is likely that getting a dateOfEvent assertion
assertions.certainty_reason: The assertions define the term in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper gives ChemicalReaction as a lower-ontology example: a subcollection of PhysicalTransformationEvent in which two or more substances undergo chemical change, with subcollections including CombustionReaction, ExothermicReaction and Fermenting, and a strong suggestion that a catalyst be given.
quotes: Each instance of ChemicalReaction is an event in which two or more substances undergo a chemical change
(genls ExothermicReaction ChemicalReaction)
(keGenlsStrongSuggestionPreds-RelationAllExists ChemicalReaction catalyst)
assertions.certainty_reason: The assertions define the term in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper gives the catalyst predicate: (catalyst R X) means ChemicalReaction R has the quantity of substance X as a catalyst; arg1Isa is ChemicalReaction, arg2Isa is PartiallyTangible, and enzymes are capable of being catalysts in chemical reactions.
quotes: (catalyst R X) means that the ChemicalReaction R has the particular quantity of substance X as a catalyst.
(arg1Isa catalyst ChemicalReaction)
Enzymes are capable of being catalysts in chemical reactions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The assertions define the predicate in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper states that each instance of CombustionReaction is a rapid chemical reaction that produces a flame, with outputsCreated-TypeType CombustionReaction Flame.
quotes: Each instance of CombustionReaction is a rapid chemical reaction that produces a flame.
assertions.certainty_reason: The comment assertion defines the term.

assertions.value: The paper presents a partial CycL representation of Martin Luther burning a papal bull in Wittenburg on 10 December 1520 as a test that the KB can describe a novel event, using preexisting terms, with BurningOfPapalBull as a SocialGathering and at least forty university students attending.
quotes: The true test of the significance of repository of knowledge is whether it can be used to describe a novel event
(dateOfEvent BurningOfPapalBull (DayFn 10 (MonthFn December (YearFn 1520))))
At least forty university students attended the event.
assertions.reader_inference: One worked example, with no evaluation on other events or by other users.

papers.title_in_file: Experimental demonstration of interaction-free all-optical switching via the quantum Zeno effect
papers.what_it_is: A 2013 arXiv letter reporting a chi-2 Fabry-Perot cavity switch, with difference-frequency generation as the pump interaction, that the authors call interaction-free via the quantum Zeno effect, with a measured on/off contrast of 35:1 and a zero-parameter model.

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental all-optical interaction-free switch based on the quantum Zeno effect with a switching contrast of 35:1, measured as the ratio of signal power transmitted by the cavity with the pump off to that with the pump on.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Section on typical switching performance, p.3
quotes: We experimentally demonstrate all-optical interaction-free switching using the quantum Zeno eﬀect, achieving a high contrast of 35:1.
The ratio between the transmitted
power when the pump is oﬀ to that when it is on is 35,
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The 35:1 figure is a transmitted-power ratio on one cavity at one pump setting, not a measured error rate or extinction over many runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that the headline switching performance figure was taken with both the signal and the DF fields on resonance, with a pump pulse width of 20 ns and a peak power of 17 W; the theory curves are zero-parameter predictions, not fits.
quotes: Experimental switching performance when both the signal and DF ﬁelds are on resonance
Note the theory curves are not ﬁts, but zeroparameter predictions.
Pump pulse width is 20 ns with a peak power of 17 W.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own operating conditions in the Fig. 2 caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that their experimental data match a zero-parameter theoretical model for several different regimes of operation, because the model parameters were measured directly and left no free parameters for the switching behavior.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Section on the model, p.2; Section on switching performance, p.3
quotes: The experimental data matches a zero-parameter theoretical model for several diﬀerent regimes of operation
The parameters in these equations can be directly measured, leaving no free parameters for describing the experimental performance of the switch.
All of our experimental data are in good agreement with the predictions of the theory without the need for any ﬁtting parameter.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical agreement reported by the authors from one study; the match is shown in figures and described as good, not quantified in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper itself reports two departures from the model (higher pump power needed, about 3% residual transmission), so the agreement is qualitative in places.

assertions.value: The authors state that they implement a recently proposed protocol and, for the first time, demonstrate high-contrast all-optical switching based on the quantum Zeno effect.
quotes: In this Letter, we describe implementation of a recently-proposed protocol [7, 8] and for the ﬁrst time demonstrate high-contrast all-optical switching based on the quantum Zeno eﬀect.
In summary, we have demonstrated, for the ﬁrst time, interaction-free all-optical switching with high contrast (35:1).
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper also describes a prior two-photon-absorption switching result at very low contrast, so first applies to high contrast.

assertions.value: The authors describe the mechanism: with the pump on, the signal field that enters the cavity is converted to the DF field, so constructive interference is inhibited and the photon is prevented from entering the cavity.
quotes: With the pump on, however, the signal ﬁeld that enters the cavity
is converted to the DF ﬁeld, so constructive interference is inhibited, and the photon is prevented from entering the cavity.
assertions.certainty_reason: A qualitative mechanism description supported by the later model and data.

assertions.value: The authors state that, from the Zeno perspective, the pump is constantly measuring whether the photon is in the cavity, which guarantees that the photon will not enter the cavity and instead will be reflected.
quotes: From the Zeno perspective, the pump is constantly measuring if the photon is in the cavity, which guarantees that the photon will not enter the cavity
assertions.certainty_reason: An interpretive statement by the authors, with no separate test of the Zeno interpretation in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The measured 35:1 contrast and the zero-parameter model do not by themselves separate a Zeno reading from a classical interference reading of the same cavity.

assertions.value: The authors state that a Zeno-based switch mediated by an interaction-free process has no direct coupling, so loss is minimized and decoherence from signal-pump coupling is eliminated, making it suitable for quantum as well as classical signals.
quotes: In contrast, a Zeno-based switch mediated via an interaction-free process has no direct coupling, so the loss is minimized and the decoherence from signal-pump coupling is eliminated, making it suitable for working with quantum as well as classical signals.
assertions.certainty_reason: A motivating claim by the authors; the experiment used a classical CW HeNe signal.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum-state signal was switched in this paper, so the suitability for quantum signals is untested here.

assertions.value: The authors describe the prototype as a Fabry-Perot cavity with an intracavity crystal phase-matched for difference-frequency generation, resonant with a high finesse at both the signal and difference frequencies but not at the pump frequency.
quotes: The prototype switch presented in this letter is based on a Fabry-Pérot design (see Fig. 1(a)) with an intracavity crystal phase-matched for diﬀerence-frequency (DF) generation
The cavity is resonant with a high ﬁnesse at both the signal and the diﬀerence frequencies (but not at the pump frequency for this implementation;
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device design.

assertions.value: The authors state that a high finesse for the pump would decrease the required pump power.
quotes: a high ﬁnesse for the pump would decrease the required pump power
assertions.certainty_reason: An untested design remark by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report a CW Helium-Neon laser at 633 nm as the signal, a 1550-nm pulse made by chopping a CW laser with an electro-optic modulator and amplifying it with an erbium-doped fiber amplifier, and a cavity of two curved mirrors (radii of curvature of 75 mm, separated by about 25 mm) around a 5-mm-long periodically poled lithium-niobate crystal phase-matched for DF generation at 1070 nm.
quotes: We use the output from a CW Helium-Neon laser at 633 nm as the signal with a 1550-nm pulse created by chopping the output of a CW laser with an electro-optic modulator
and then amplifying it with an erbium-doped ﬁber ampliﬁer.

The cavity is made up of two curved mirrors (radii of curvature of 75 mm, separated by about 25 mm) around a 5-mm-long lithium-niobate crystal, which is periodically poled for quasi-phase-matched DF generation at 1070 nm.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own apparatus.

assertions.value: The authors state that the implementation is a modified version of an earlier proposal; the primary difference is a continuous-wave signal beam used for experimental convenience, with the pump still pulsed.
quotes: The implementation presented in this Letter is a modiﬁed version of the proposal developed in [8].
we use a continuous-wave (CW) signal beam for experimental convenience
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how its experiment departs from the proposal it implements.
assertions.reader_inference: A CW signal is not a single-photon or pulsed-signal test of the protocol; the switch was operated on a classical beam.

assertions.value: The authors model the switch by quasi-static analysis, valid if all input intensities vary slowly with respect to the cavity round-trip time, and for the nonlinear crystal assume a single-mode regime, perfect phase-matching, and an undepleted pump.
quotes: The switch is modeled here using quasi-static analysis, similar to the usual classical description of a Fabry-Pérot cavity, which is valid if all of the input intensities vary slowly with respect to the cavity round-trip time.
assuming a single-mode regime, perfect phase-matching, and an undepleted pump
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the conditions under which its model holds.

assertions.value: The authors define the cavity finesse as the ratio of the free-spectral range to the bandwidth.
quotes: The values of the cavity ﬁnesse (ratio of the free-spectral range to the bandwidth)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the term where it first uses it.

assertions.value: The authors report that, when slightly off resonance at the signal frequency, the pump can effectively shift the cavity resonance, either increasing or decreasing the cavity transmission depending on the phase shift of the DF, and that when significantly off resonance at the DF there is effectively no change in cavity behavior when the pump is turned on; the theory curves have no fitting parameters.
assertions.anchor: Section on off-resonant conditions, p.3; Fig. 3 caption
quotes: When slightly oﬀ-resonance at the signal frequency, the pump can effectively shift the cavity resonance, either increasing (a) or decreasing (b) the cavity transmission, depending on the phase shift of the DF.
When signiﬁcantly oﬀ resonance at the DF (c), there is eﬀectively no change in the cavity behavior when the pump is turned on.
All theory curves have no ﬁtting parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one apparatus, shown in Fig. 3.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing their earlier theory work, that if the cavity is very lossy at the difference frequency, much more pump power is required for switching and the cavity resonance at the signal frequency is destroyed rather than shifted.
quotes: theory predicts that much more pump power is required for switching, and the cavity resonance at the signal frequency is destroyed (rather than shifted) [8].
assertions.certainty_reason: A theory prediction the paper attributes to earlier work.

the switching contrast is signiﬁcantly lower (1.6:1 compared to 35:1)

assertions.reader_inference: A low-loss difference-frequency path is the design requirement for high contrast; the 35:1 result does not hold without it.

quotes: we are able to look at diﬀerent relative values of φD and verify that the switching contrast does not change, as predicted.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one apparatus.

assertions.value: The authors state that the switching is not very dependent on the pump power: as pump power increases, the cavity rapidly becomes highly reflective and then saturates, until g approaches 2π at a pump power of about 80 kW; the pump-power figure shows the doubly-resonant case, and the authors present closed-form steady-state transmission and reflection coefficients for double resonance (the equations are garbled in the text layer).

quotes: One feature of this device is that the switching is not very dependent on the pump power.
we can solve for the steady-state transmission and reﬂection coeﬃcients of the cavity when on double resonance, i.e.,
As the pump power increases, the cavity rapidly becomes highly reﬂective, and then saturates (until g approaches 2π, at a pump power of about 80 kW).
The switching does not depend on pump power beyond a certain threshold, making the device less sensitive to pump ﬂuctuations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A model result and a measured curve over the available power range; the saturation regime near 80 kW was not tested.
assertions.reader_inference: The measured powers reached 150 W, far below the 80 kW saturation point quoted from the model, so the saturation regime is a model prediction, not a measurement.

assertions.value: The authors report that significantly more pump power is required to switch the light if the cavity is high-loss at the DF, and that the regime in which it is expected to saturate is not accessible with the components used.

When the cavity is lossy at the DF, the pump power required for switching is much higher.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result with a stated experimental limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the switching takes more power to turn on than their zero-parameter single-spatial-mode model predicts, and that about 3% residual transmitted light is seen where the model predicts a value much closer to zero; they offer spatial mode mismatch as one possible explanation and name resolving the discrepancies as a goal of future investigation.
quotes: Note that the switching takes more power to turn on than is predicted with our zero-parameter single-spatial-mode model.
Such spatial mismatch is also a possible explanation for the ∼3% residual transmitted light when the model predicts a value much closer to zero.
Resolving these discrepancies will be one goal of our future investigation.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical departure from the model with an untested explanation.
assertions.reader_inference: The residual transmission of about 3% bounds the contrast of this prototype; the claimed zero-parameter match therefore does not hold at the low-transmission end.

assertions.value: The authors state that they performed systematic studies of the switching in three operational regimes (intracavity DF resonant, detuned from resonance, and subjected to high intracavity loss), that all three lead to interaction-free switching observed in both the reflected and transmitted ports, and that the best performance was with both signal and DF fields in cavity resonance.
quotes: we have performed systematic studies of this switching mechanism in three separate operational regimes, corresponding to where the intracavity DF is resonant with the cavity, detuned from the cavity resonance, and subjected to high intracavity loss.
All three cases lead to interaction-free switching, which was observed by measuring the signal power present in both the reﬂected and the transmitted ports of the device.
The best performance, however, was achieved when both the signal and the DF ﬁelds are in cavity resonance.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' conclusion from one set of experiments.
assertions.reader_inference: The lossy-DF regime reached only 1.6:1, so calling it interaction-free switching rests on the authors' definition, not on high contrast.

assertions.value: The authors state that other Zeno-based all-optical switching protocols have been proposed using two-photon absorption in rubidium vapor and inverse-Raman scattering in silicon microresonators, that the inverse-Raman scheme has been demonstrated for modulation only and not switching, and that initial evidence of two-photon-absorption switching was recently observed at very low contrast, with signal transmission affected by about 3%.
quotes: (which has been demonstrated for modulation only, not switching [12])
Initial evidence of the TPA-induced switching has been recently observed with very low contrast, where the signal transmission through the switch was shown to be aﬀected by about 3% [13, 14].
assertions.certainty_reason: Results the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that, by using a microresonator instead of bulk optics, such a switch can operate with ultra-low energies, potentially down to the single-photon level, and can act as an optical transistor in which a lower-energy pulse switches a higher-energy pulse.
quotes: such a switch can operate with ultra-low energies (potentially down to the single-photon level) and can even act as an optical transistor, i.e., a lower-energy pulse can switch a higher-energy pulse.
assertions.certainty_reason: A projection by the authors; the prototype used bulk optics and a 17 W peak pump.

assertions.value: The authors state that a lithium-niobate microdisk with a 1-mm diameter and Q > 107 (exponent printed flat in the text layer) could achieve low-loss (<10%) switching with pump-pulse energy on the order of 10 pJ, and that tailored pump pulses with smaller microdisks and higher Q could further reduce the pump-pulse energy to single-photon energy, leading to deterministic quantum logic gates for single-photon signals.
quotes: using a lithium-niobate microdisk with a 1-mm diameter and Q > 107, whose fabrication and operation has been well demonstrated [15, 16], low loss (<10%) switching can be achieved with pump-pulse energy on the order of 10 pJ.
the pump-pulse energy could be further reduced to single-photon energy, leading to deterministic quantum logic gates for single-photon signals [17].
assertions.certainty_reason: A projection by the authors, not tested in this paper; the single-photon gate work is cited as submitted.
assertions.reader_inference: Nothing in the paper measures a microdisk device or a single-photon signal.
